scholarships.title: DAAD Research Grants in Germany (for doctoral candidates and early postdocs)

existing.description: The DAAD Research Grants in Germany fund a research project at a state or state-recognised university or non-university research institute in Germany, carried out with a German scientific supervisor. Doctoral candidates may be funded for 2 to 12 months and early postdocs for 2 to 6 months; the grant cannot be extended and cannot be split within the funding period. The current DAAD announcement sets a monthly scholarship payment of EUR 1,400 plus insurance cover, a travel allowance, and for stays over six months a research allowance of EUR 460, a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly family allowance. Applications are submitted online through the DAAD Portal and are open annually, with deadlines updated in the second quarter of each year; on 2026-10-04 the DAAD stated that applications for the 2027 funding period were closed.
eligibility: Doctoral students: the start of the doctorate should not be more than 3 years ago at the application deadline
Postdocs: the doctorate should not have been completed more than 4 years before the application deadline
Doing the doctorate at a university or research institution outside Germany; applicants doing their entire doctorate at a German university cannot apply
Research project at a state or state-recognised university or a non-university research institute in Germany, agreed with a German scientific supervisor
Not resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline
For applicants in human medicine, veterinary medicine and dentistry, further subject-specific regulations apply
existing.eligibility_summary: Doctoral candidates whose doctorate started no more than 3 years before the application deadline, or postdocs who completed their doctorate no more than 4 years before the deadline, who are doing their doctorate outside Germany, with a German host institution and supervisor.
benefits: Health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Research allowance of EUR 460 per month for stays over six months
Monthly rent subsidy for stays over six months
Monthly allowance for accompanying family members for stays over six months
German language course support, including online course fees and a personally chosen course allowance, for stays over six months
Green Mobility Top Up or reimbursement of carbon offset payments
coverage: Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover
Travel allowance, with an application required if the funding period exceeds six months
Research allowance of EUR 460 for a funding period of more than six months
Monthly rent subsidy, only for a funding period of more than six months
Monthly allowance for accompanying family members, only for a funding period of more than six months
Green Mobility Top Up for climate-friendly travel, or reimbursement of carbon offset payments for air travel
Payment of course fees for an online language course, and if necessary a German language course in Germany before the project starts, only for a funding period of more than six months
Reimbursement of the fee for a TestDaF or DSH test, only for a funding period of more than six months
Individual subsidy for justified additional costs in the case of a disability or chronic illness, on application
requirements: Submit the application online through the DAAD Portal; only PDF files can be uploaded
Documents in a national language must be accompanied by a German or English translation
Applications are valid only if all required documents are submitted by the deadline; incomplete applications cannot be considered
Indicate the desired funding period in the application form; the funding period is determined by the selection committee and the scholarship cannot be extended
Research work in countries other than Germany is not eligible for funding, and the funding cannot be divided within the funding period
Benefit from third parties is partially credited towards the DAAD scholarship
documents: Full curriculum vitae in tabular form, maximum 3 pages
List of published publications, maximum 10 pages; mandatory for postdocs
Letter of motivation of 1 to 2 pages explaining the academic and personal reasons for the planned research project in Germany
Research proposal of a maximum of 10 pages, prepared by the applicant and discussed with the German academic adviser
Time schedule of the planned research work
Proof of admission to or enrolment in doctoral studies, for doctoral candidates
Confirmation from the academic host in Germany guaranteeing a workplace at the host institute
Declaration from the scientific supervisor in Germany on safety-relevant and ethical aspects of the research project
All university degree certificates already obtained, with final grades, or a provisional document if the latest certificate is not yet available
Transcripts of records for undergraduate and postgraduate programmes showing individual grades
One recent supporting letter of recommendation on a DAAD form from a university teacher, for doctoral candidates from the doctoral supervisor
existing.english_requirement: The application and all documents are handled in German or English; documents in another national language need a German or English translation. Selection takes account of knowledge of the language of instruction or working language, and German language skills are assessed if different from the working language.
application_method: Online application through the DAAD Portal, after registering
Generate the recommendation form in the DAAD Portal under 'Create Letter of Recommendation Form' during the application period
existing.selection_notes: An independent selection committee of specialist scientists reviews applications. The selection criteria are academic qualification (grade point average, development of grades, academic progress, language knowledge, scholarly achievements after graduation), quality of the research project (originality, topicality and relevance, choice of host institution and first contacts, feasibility and consistency of the study plan and schedule, integration within the overall doctorate), and the applicant's potential (career prospects, motivation, non-study-related activities). The committee also gives due consideration to equal opportunities.
existing.best_fit: Doctoral candidates from any country, at any institution outside Germany, in the first three years of a doctorate, and early postdocs within four years of completing their doctorate, who can secure a German host institute and supervisor and want a 2 to 12 month research stay in Germany.
existing.notes: The doctorate itself is awarded by the home university; the German stay is a research phase, not a complete doctorate. The funding period must begin in 2027 for the current round. DAAD lektoren in many countries can advise applicants before they apply.
existing.duration: 2 to 12 months for doctoral candidates; 2 to 6 months for postdocs
existing.application_period: Annual cycle. The DAAD portal opens at least six weeks before the deadline and closes at 24:00 CET or CEST on the last application day. For the 2027 funding round the applications were closed on the 2026-10-04 verification date.
existing.deadline_display: "Application deadlines are updated annually in the second quarter. In most cases, they are in the same period as the previous year." The DAAD page for the 2027 funding period showed "Currently you cannot apply for this programme" on 2026-10-04; the exact calendar date was not rendered on the page read.
existing.program_type: Research stay grant for doctoral candidates and early postdocs

scholarships.title: DAAD University Summer Courses offered in Germany for Foreign Students and Graduates (HSK)

existing.description: The DAAD University Summer Courses programme funds four-week German language, cultural studies and technical language courses at German universities and affiliated language schools for students and graduates from eligible countries. The scholarship covers the cost of the language course, provides accommodation in a single room through the course provider for the duration of the course, pays a one-time allowance of EUR 475, a country-specific travel allowance, and health, accident and personal liability insurance. Applications are accepted each year from 1 September to 30 October at 23:59 Central European Time, and courses run between June and September.
eligibility: Applications are open to students and graduates in any subject area

Undergraduate students must have completed at least two academic years of university study by the time the funding period begins; final-year students are eligible only if they intend to undertake postgraduate study immediately after graduating
Must be at least 18 years old when starting the language course
Must be enrolled at a university in one of the programme-related countries, excluding Germany, both at the time of application and throughout the entire scholarship period
Must be able to follow lectures in German and participate in group work, with German language proficiency proven at the time of application
Funding from the programme can only be claimed once
existing.eligibility_summary: Students and graduates in any subject area from a list of programme countries, enrolled at a university in a programme country other than Germany at the time of application and throughout the scholarship, aged at least 18 at the start of the course, with proven German language skills.
benefits: Full coverage of the language course fees
Single-room accommodation arranged by the course provider for the whole course
Health, accident and personal liability insurance
coverage: Costs of the German language course
Accommodation in a single room provided by the course provider for the duration of the course, such as a student dormitory, shared apartment or private household
One-time allowance of EUR 475, paid in cash on site by the course provider
Health, accident and personal liability insurance benefits
requirements: Applications must be submitted online through the DAAD Portal; only PDF files can be uploaded
Applicants must name three courses in the application form at three different course locations, and the DAAD reserves the right to assign a different course if capacities are limited
Course preferences cannot be changed and courses cannot be switched once the application has been received
Participation is exclusively in person; remote participation is not possible, and the courses are taught exclusively in German
The German language certificate must not be older than one year at the time of application, except B2 or TDN3 certificates in all examination parts, which may be up to two years old
Incomplete applications cannot be considered; the DAAD portal closes at 24:00 CET or CEST on the last application day
documents: Online application form
Complete curriculum vitae in tabular form, in German
Letter of motivation, in German
Transcripts of all university examinations taken in the last two consecutive years, including individual grades, in the original and with a German or English translation

If no transcript for the past two years is available because of a shorter period of study, proof of academic achievements for the current period of study together with the school-leaving certificate including individual grades, in the original and with a German or English translation
For graduates, the last university degree certificate with the final grade, in the original and with a German or English translation
German language certificates, with a German or English translation where applicable
Other documents considered important, such as proof of internships or employment certificates, with translations where applicable
For final-year undergraduates, a certificate from the university confirming the intention to undertake postgraduate study, or a clear statement of that intention in the application documents
application_method: Online application through the DAAD Portal between 1 September and 30 October each year
existing.selection_notes: A selection committee reviews all applications. The key selection criteria are previous academic achievements and a convincing letter of motivation for the choice of study programme and future academic project.
existing.best_fit: Undergraduate students who have completed at least two years of study, and graduates, from any subject area, who are enrolled at a university in a programme country other than Germany and need German language study at an intermediate or higher level.
existing.notes: The courses run for four weeks between June and September, and the grants are not extendable. The DAAD transfers the one-time allowance and any travel allowance to the course provider, who disburses it in cash to scholarship holders on site, so those amounts are not paid into a bank account abroad. Accepted language certificates are onSET-Deutsch, TestDaF, Goethe Institut Zertifikat, DSD, DSH, telc Deutsch and OSD-Zertifikat; for subject-specific language courses the Abitur is also accepted as proof of German proficiency.
existing.duration: 4 weeks (maximum 5 days per week, at least 25 teaching hours per week)
existing.application_period: 1 September to 30 October each year; applications for the 2027 courses close at 23:59 CET on 30 October 2026.
existing.deadline_display: "30 October of each year, 23:59 (Central European Time). Applications are possible from 01 September each year"
existing.program_type: Short-term German language and cultural studies summer course grant (Hochschul-Sommerkurse, HSK)
